gs_mapping: GS III - Environment, Climate Change, Energy and Sustainable Development

knowledge_points.title: Cleaner Energy Sources
knowledge_points.text: Solar and other renewable power can support growing energy needs while reducing dependence on more polluting sources. The article links this shift with new investment and manufacturing opportunities.

knowledge_points.title: Using Less Energy
knowledge_points.text: Efficient lights, buildings and industries deliver useful services with less energy. This lowers waste and emissions while allowing homes and businesses to use resources more productively.

knowledge_points.title: Cleaner Industrial Production
knowledge_points.text: Green hydrogen can help industries such as steel and fertilisers reduce emissions. Building this sector can also create work in equipment, renewable power, storage and transport.

knowledge_points.title: Saving Water And Materials
knowledge_points.text: Water reuse, efficient irrigation and recycling reduce pressure on limited resources. A circular economy keeps materials useful longer instead of treating them only as waste.

knowledge_points.title: Resilient Cities And Communities
knowledge_points.text: Better public transport, green buildings and urban wetlands can improve city life. Planning for floods, heat and water shortages also helps protect development from climate risks.

quick_facts.text: The National Solar Mission began in 2010 to advance solar energy. The PLI scheme supports domestic manufacturing of high-efficiency solar photovoltaic modules.
PAT targets energy-intensive industries, while the Energy Conservation Building Code and Eco Niwas Samhita address buildings. Efficient lighting also helps reduce energy demand.
The National Green Hydrogen Mission targets 5 million metric tonnes annually by 2030, supported by approximately 125 GW renewable capacity and Rs 19,744 crore.

Extended Producer Responsibility addresses plastics and electronic waste, including recycling. Mission LiFE promotes responsible mobility, while adaptation includes early warnings, resilient agriculture and water security.

key_takeaway: India can pursue green growth through renewable energy, efficiency, cleaner industry, recycling and climate-resilient cities, supporting economic development while reducing environmental harm.
